note: Conscious non-coverage for the Clinical Procedures Pipeline standards baseline at programme open (Wave 0.4). Four entries are COVERED_ELSEWHERE rather than deferred: device traceability, transfusion practice and critical-result acknowledgement are genuinely implemented, just not as governed content this generator can see. Those entries name what is real and what is still missing inside them, because a COVERED_ELSEWHERE that hides a gap is worse than a deferral.

exclusions.reason: P11 seeded IPC-HAND_HYGIENE as a real procedure_requirement row (kind IPC) across all 66 published catalogue entries — every invasive procedure in this catalogue qualifies by construction. Each row has a named owner (PERFORMING_CLINICIAN), a mandatory obligation and a BLOCK on-unavailable action, the same readiness-engine shape every other requirement in this schema uses — not a generic checkbox. Not visible to this generator because it is a SQL seed row, not CKP content JSON with a dakRef.
exclusions.revisitCondition: None expected for the requirement's existence. Would need revisiting if this generator gains a non-CKP coverage path for procedures-service's own migration content.

exclusions.reason: P11 broadened V003's two-procedure IPC-ASEPTIC seed to all 66 catalogue entries, and added IPC-PPE and IPC-SKIN_PREP as separate requirement rows (kind IPC) — the three items the audit named together (aseptic technique, PPE, skin preparation) are now each a real, named-owner requirement rather than absent. The surgical baseline's own SSI.2018.PREOPERATIVE standard, where it also covers skin preparation, still needs its own S13 rules to REFERENCE this content rather than duplicate it — that cross-reference is not built yet.
exclusions.revisitCondition: S13 ships surgical-site-infection rules that reference IPC-SKIN_PREP rather than re-declaring skin preparation.

exclusions.reason: P11 closed the specific gap the previous DEFERRED entry named — declared reprocessing limits — with CSSD-REPROCESSING_LIMITS (kind STERILE_PROCESSING), seeded for every catalogue entry whose permitted settings include THEATRE or ENDOSCOPY (49 rows), on top of tuso.instrument_set_cssd_cycle and inpatient.procedure_instrument_set_use, which already gave an instrument set a traceable sterilisation cycle. Single-use item discipline is covered under IPC-INJECTION_SAFETY below rather than duplicated here. STILL ABSENT, and not claimed: environmental cleaning between procedures has nowhere to go in this schema at all.
exclusions.revisitCondition: A future wave adds environmental cleaning as its own requirement kind or content — no plan for it yet.

exclusions.reason: P11 seeded IPC-INJECTION_SAFETY (kind IPC, all 66 procedures) declaring single-use device discipline, immediate exposure-incident reporting and clinical waste segregation as a real, named-owner requirement — the obligation now exists where it previously had nowhere to go. STILL ABSENT, and not claimed: this is the requirement's DECLARATION only (content, engine-not-store, matching this programme's own boundary — see the P10 lease entry). The EXECUTION half — an actual exposure incident routed to Rito as a staff safety event — is inpatient-service's to build, the same content/execution split P8 drew for specimens and implants.
exclusions.revisitCondition: inpatient-service (or a future wave here) wires an actual exposure-incident report to RitoSafetyClient, the same routing pattern procedure_safety_event already uses for other incident categories.

exclusions.reason: This is the most serious gap in the pipeline audit and it deserves to be stated plainly. Site and side are recorded on a surgical referral and are shown on the theatre case banner, but nothing verifies them: there is no site marking, no structured laterality on the procedure episode, and no gate that refuses to start a procedure whose site and side were not confirmed. The WHO Time Out asks the question; the platform has no field that can hold the answer.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P4 puts structured site and side on the procedure episode with a start gate, and P7 makes confirmation an explicit safety-pause step for every class where laterality or multiple structures apply.

exclusions.reason: Harm is recorded but not managed. procedure_safety_event routes to Rito, which is real and more than most systems have, but the action plan's expectation is that harm is engineered out by design and that patients and families are engaged — and there is no disclosure or open-communication path to a patient at all.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P10 ships the complication model including disclosure and communication to the patient, with the Rito review link preserved.

exclusions.reason: A consent bundle exists and is genuinely good: procedure, anaesthesia and transfusion consent are separate, theatre start is hard-gated on GRANTED, and an audited emergency exception path exists with two-doctor, deferred and proxy variants. What is absent is the content of the conversation — purpose, benefits, material risks, alternatives, consequences of no procedure, questions asked, language and interpreter. Consent today records that consent happened, which is exactly the reduction to a signature the specification forbids.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P5 ships the consent content fields in mvumo and the pipeline refuses to treat a consent record with no recorded discussion as informed.

exclusions.plannedWave: P5 (partial) — closure owned by the TSHEPO trust lane
exclusions.reason: P5 SHIPPED the substance of this standard: capacity assessment with a three-valued outcome (not-assessed is not has-capacity), guardian consent requiring a recorded basis, child assent as an act distinct from guardian consent so a child's refusal is representable, substitute decision-making, refusal and withdrawal as an actor-and-time pair. What remains PARTIAL is adolescent confidentiality alone, and for a platform reason rather than effort: SPECIALLY_PROTECTED now has a real classifier and a protected-lane marker check, but still resolves to the same DataVisibilityTier as ordinary clinical data (ResourceSensitivityClassifier line 93). A separate lane ending in a shared tier is a label, not a boundary — so an adolescent told their consent is confidential would be told something the system does not keep.
exclusions.revisitCondition: SPECIALLY_PROTECTED resolves to a distinct DataVisibilityTier, caregiver context is a first-class PDP input, and both access and refusal are audited. Trust-plane work, not this programme's to complete.

exclusions.reason: Genuinely implemented, and more completely than the first pass of the audit credited. inventory-service holds a national implant registry — ImplantTraceabilityService over ImplantUnitEntity and PatientImplantEntity — exposing recall trace by UDI or lot across all patients, per-patient implant history and per-unit history, with product, manufacturer, lot, serial, expiry and site captured at insertion. Not visible to this generator because it is Java and SQL rather than governed content. Two real gaps remain inside the standard: information given to the patient about their own implant, and removal, revision or replacement as tracked events.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P8 ships patient-facing implant information and the removal/revision lifecycle; S11 extends the same registry to drains and stomas as longitudinal objects.

exclusions.reason: Implemented across MADI and the theatre blood gate: a procedure's blood requirement is checked against a real MADI reservation with compatibility, readiness blocks when blood is required and not reserved, and transfusion is recorded against the episode. Consent for transfusion is separately captured. The gap is the bedside step the standard cares most about: positive patient identification at the point of administration, and structured observation during transfusion.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P7 ships transfusion as a procedure class with its own safety pause including bedside positive identification, and observation during administration.

exclusions.reason: Anaesthesia is modelled as a specialty activity with ASA classification, airway assessment, a time-series chart and a scoring engine. Sedation as a continuum of depth is not modelled at all, which matters because the standard's whole point is that requirements follow the depth that may be reached rather than the depth intended — so a moderate-sedation endoscopy needs deep-sedation rescue capability available.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P7 ships the seven sedation levels with monitoring, provider competence, rescue capability and recovery criteria derived from the level.

exclusions.reason: The anaesthesia chart can record pulse oximetry and the WHO checklist Sign In includes it, so the data path exists. What does not exist is the assertion: nothing refuses to proceed when mandatory monitoring is unavailable, and nothing checks that a trained anaesthesia provider is present for the depth of sedation planned.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P7 makes mandatory monitoring and provider presence readiness requirements that block, with an audited emergency override rather than a silent bypass.

exclusions.reason: The specimen path from a procedure to a histopathology report is real and end to end: inpatient.procedure_specimen to OROS lab specimens to a histopathology report, with the surgical discharge summary surfacing results still pending. Chain of custody specifically is thin — collector, container, fixative, destination and receipt exist in places, but there is no custody transfer record and nothing prevents an unlabelled or mismatched specimen, which is the failure the standard exists to stop.
exclusions.revisitCondition: P8 ships custody transfer and label verification such that an unlabelled specimen cannot be accepted.

exclusions.reason: Implemented in OROS and stronger than the audit's first pass suggested. The order lifecycle distinguishes preliminary, final, released, acknowledged, amended and superseded states, result escalation exists, and a notification consumer for critical results was enabled by the trauma stream. Not visible here because the states are Java enums, not governed content. The gap is not acknowledgement itself but its consequence: nothing prevents a clinical episode closing while a required result sits unacknowledged.
exclusions.revisitCondition: S10 makes the surgical episode refuse to close on an unreviewed histology result, using the existing ACKNOWLEDGED state as the gate.

exclusions.reason: Fully implemented as governed content in procedures.clavien_dindo_grade (all seven grades, real literature citation) and procedures.complication_class (typical_grade_code resolved against it, proven to reject an invented grade). Not visible to this generator because this standard is not a WHO DAK artefact at all — it is a peer-reviewed surgical-literature classification (Dindo, Demartines, Clavien, Ann Surg 2004), declared in this domain's own standards-baseline.json rather than extracted from a WHO source under docs/reference/who-dak/. The generator's SHIPPED detection only recognises CKP content JSON carrying dakRef+adaptation, which does not apply to a non-DAK standard implemented directly in procedures-service's own migration content.
exclusions.revisitCondition: None expected — this is complete as implemented. Would only need revisiting if the traceability generator gains a non-DAK coverage path, at which point this entry could flip to SHIPPED instead of COVERED_ELSEWHERE.
